symbols.type: normalized positive alternating calibration right factor
symbols.def: \(v^{\mathrm{cal}}_t=p^{\mathrm{alt}}_t/\sqrt{T(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)}\) for the even values of \(T\) used by the calibration array

symbols.name: cloc
symbols.role: fixed lower bound for every target-specific restricted signal

symbols.name: zinnov
symbols.type: Gaussian innovation array for the rank-one calibration family

symbols.name: Pr
symbols.sig: \(\mathcal P_r:\mathbb R^{\mathcal I\times\mathcal J}\to\mathbb R^{\mathcal I\times\mathcal J}\) for finite ordered index sets \(\mathcal I\) and \(\mathcal J\)
symbols.def: A measurable Frobenius-best rank-\(r\) projection with deterministic singular-vector tie breaking.

symbols.name: Iit
symbols.def: \(I_{it}=C(t)\cup\{i\}\), equipped with the increasing deterministic ordering inherited from \(I\)

symbols.name: Jit
symbols.def: \(J_{it}=S\cup\{t\}\), equipped with the increasing deterministic ordering inherited from \(J\)

symbols.name: Rit
symbols.def: \(R_{it}(E)=(E_{ju})_{j\in I_{it},u\in J_{it}}\) in the fixed orderings of \(I_{it}\) and \(J_{it}\)

symbols.name: Olocal
symbols.def: \(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}=\Omega\cap(I_{it}\times J_{it})=C(t)\times(S\cup\{t\})\;\cup\;\{i\}\times S\), expressed in the fixed local chart

symbols.name: Ecoord
symbols.def: \(E^{it}_{ju}\) is the canonical basis matrix with one in local coordinate \((j,u)\) and zero elsewhere in the fixed ordered local space

symbols.name: Mtilde

symbols.sig: \(\widetilde M^{it}\in\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\) for \((i,t)\in G\times W\)

symbols.name: ellhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\ell_{it}\) is obtained from \(\ell_{it}\) by using the rank-\(r\) singular factors of \(\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})\) in the same ordered local chart

symbols.name: qhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat q_{it}(e)=[\widehat Q_{it}(e+\widehat\ell_{it}(e)E^{it}_{it})]_{it}/(1-\widehat h_{it})\) in the fixed ordered local chart

symbols.name: phasefrontier
symbols.role: derived by Open-ended Question 1 over the exponent-indexed class

symbols.name: P

assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that \(cn\le N,T\le Cn\) for every \(n\).
There are constants \(0<c_G<C_G<1\) such that \(c_Gn\le g\le C_Gn\).

novel.justification: A policy experiment that assigns a fixed positive share of eligible securities to treatment generates this regime; the SEC Tick Size Pilot has precisely a cohort-level intervention rather than isolated treated cells.

assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c_S<C_S<1\) such that \(c_Sn\le m\le C_Sn\).
There are constants \(0<c_C<C_C<1\) such that \(c_Cn\le |C(t)|\le C_Cn\) uniformly over \(t\in W\).
The set \(W\) is an interval in \(J\).
The sets satisfy \(\max S<\min W\).
There is a constant \(c_W\in(0,1)\) such that \(1\le H\le(1-c_W)T\).

standard.name: post-window length below the full time dimension

assumptions.condition: The integer \(r\) is fixed and known.
The signal satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\).
The integer \(q\) is fixed and known.
The treatment matrix satisfies \(A_{it}=1\{i\in G,t\in W\}\).
The untreated observation set \(\Omega\) is nonrandom.
The untreated potential outcomes obey \(Y_{it}(0)=M_{it}+\epsilon_{it}\).
The observed outcomes obey \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}=A_{it}Y_{it}(1)+(1-A_{it})Y_{it}(0)\).
For a fixed constant \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\in(0,1]\), every local signal block satisfies \(\sigma_r(M^{it})\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\) for \((i,t)\in G\times W\).

novel.justification: A fixed local-to-global signal ratio holds when donor and pretreatment restrictions retain nonvanishing factor mass; balanced common-start panels with bounded positive loadings, including the displayed alternating-factor calibration, satisfy it.

assumptions.condition: Every local signal block satisfies \(\sigma_1(M^{it})/\sigma_r(M^{it})\le\kappa\).
The singular vectors satisfy \(\max\{N\max_i\|U_{i\cdot}\|_2^2,T\max_t\|V_{t\cdot}\|_2^2\}\le\mu r\).
For constants \(0<c_A<C_A<\infty\), \(c_AI_r\preceq D^{-1/2}A_tD^{-1/2}\preceq C_AI_r\) uniformly over \(t\in W\).
For constants \(0<c_B<C_B<\infty\), \(c_BI_r\preceq D^{-1/2}B_SD^{-1/2}\preceq C_BI_r\).
Conditional on \(M\), the joint row law factorizes across \(i\in I\): the sigma-fields \(\sigma(\epsilon_{it}:t\in J)\) are mutually conditionally independent.

For every row \(i\in I\) and index sets \(\mathcal A,\mathcal B\subset J\) satisfying \(\min_{u\in\mathcal A,v\in\mathcal B}|u-v|>q\), the sigma-fields \(\sigma(\epsilon_{iu}:u\in\mathcal A)\) and \(\sigma(\epsilon_{iv}:v\in\mathcal B)\) are conditionally independent given \(M\).
The errors satisfy \(\mathbb E[\epsilon_{it}\mid M]=0\) for every \((i,t)\).
The errors satisfy \(\|\epsilon_{it}\|_{\psi_2}\le K\) uniformly over \((i,t)\).
The conditional covariance is common and stationary: \(\mathbb E[\epsilon_{it}\epsilon_{is}\mid M]=\gamma(s-t)\).
There are constants \(0<c_s<C_s<\infty\) such that \(c_s/(nH)\le s^2\le C_s/(nH)\).

standard.name: long-run variance nondegeneracy with diffuse weights

assumptions.condition: The global signal obeys \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\) for a fixed \(\eta\in(0,1/4)\).

novel.justification: The regime includes bounded-incoherence rank-one panels with \(H\asymp n\) and \(\psi=n^{4/5}\) for small positive \(\eta\), so it permits factors polynomially weaker than the strong-factor singular-value order \(n\).

assumptions.condition: The penalty satisfies \(c_\lambda K\sqrt n\,\ell_n\le\lambda\le C_\lambda K\sqrt n\,\ell_n\) for constants \(0<c_\lambda<C_\lambda<\infty\).
There are constants \(0<c_g<C_g<\infty\), locally uniform when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over compact exponent sets, such that \(c_g n^b\le g\le C_g n^b\).

novel.justification: Exponent-indexed cohort growth represents policy panels ranging from a sparse but expanding treated group to a fixed treated fraction, including subgroup analyses of the SEC Tick Size Pilot.

assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c_H<C_H<\infty\), locally uniform when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over compact exponent sets, such that \(c_H n^c\le H\le C_H n^c\).

novel.justification: A polynomial window scale distinguishes short-run, intermediate, and sustained policy summaries while the existing ordering and subset conditions enforce calendar feasibility.

assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c_\psi<C_\psi<\infty\), locally uniform when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over compact exponent sets, such that \(c_\psi n^a\le\psi\le C_\psi n^a\).

novel.justification: The exponent-indexed signal scale contains weak through strong bounded-incoherence factor arrays and exposes rather than assumes the interaction between signal, cohort, and window growth.

assumptions.condition: There are constants \(0<c_v<C_v<\infty\), locally uniform over compact exponent sets, such that \(c_v\{(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\}\le s^2\le C_v\{(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\}\).

novel.justification: This nondegeneracy condition allows donor-window and treated-pre score components to determine the larger sampling scale and rules out cancellation only at the variance level.

definitions.name: Uniform deterministic-MNAR weak-signal class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P_n:P_n\text{ governs }(M_n,\epsilon_n,Y_n(0),Y_n(1),A_n,G_n,S_n,W_n)\text{ and satisfies every member property listed for }\mathcal P_n\text{ at index }n\}\)

definitions.name: Exponent-indexed signal--cohort--window class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)=\{P_n:P_n\text{ governs }(M_n,\epsilon_n,Y_n(0),Y_n(1),A_n,G_n,S_n,W_n)\text{ and satisfies every member property listed for }\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\text{ at index }n\}\).

definitions.name: Native subgroup convex estimator
definitions.construction: For each \((i,t)\in G\times W\), set \(Y^{\mathrm{obs},it}=R_{it}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}})\), choose \(\widetilde M^{it}\in\arg\min_{A\in\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}}\{\tfrac12\|P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}(Y^{\mathrm{obs},it}-A)\|_F^2+\lambda\|A\|_*\}\) by a fixed measurable rule, set \(Z^{it}=P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}Y^{\mathrm{obs},it}+P_{(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it})^c}\widetilde M^{it}\), and set \(\widehat M_{it}=[\mathcal P_r(Z^{it})]_{it}\) in that same ordered local chart.

definitions.name: Neighborhood-noise-replaced auxiliary fit
definitions.construction: For each \((i,t)\in G\times W\), form \(Y^{\mathrm{aux},it}=M^{it}+P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}(\epsilon^{(-it)})\) in \(\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\), apply the same masked nuclear-norm optimizer and rank-\(r\) projection in the identical ordered local chart as in the native estimator, and denote its target cell by \(\widehat M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\). Only the noise coordinates in row \(i\) and \(\mathcal N_q(t)\) are replaced by zero; all other rows and the row-\(i\) coordinates outside that neighborhood are retained. The resulting target-specific fit is constructed as a \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\)-measurable object.

definitions.name: Complete local tangent score
definitions.construction: For \(e\in\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\), \(\ell_{it}(e)=\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}e_{jt}+\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}e_{is}-\sum_{j\in C(t)}\sum_{s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}e_{js}\).

definitions.name: Rank-projection quadratic drift
definitions.construction: In the ordered space \(\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\), let \(Q_{it}(E)=\tfrac12D^2\mathcal P_r(M^{it})[E,E]\), \(q_{it}(e)=[Q_{it}(e+\ell_{it}(e)E^{it}_{it})]_{it}/(1-h_{it})\), \(Q=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\), and \(B_2=\mathbb E[Q\mid M,\Omega]\). Different targets may use different local spaces; only the scalar \(q_{it}(\cdot)\) is aggregated.

definitions.name: Oracle aggregate score and variance
definitions.construction: Set \(L=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\ell_{it}(R_{it}\epsilon)=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{s=1}^T w_{js}\epsilon_{js}\) and \(s^2=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^q\gamma(h)\sum_{s=1}^T w_{js}w_{j,s+h}\), with \(w_{j,u}=0\) outside \(J\).

definitions.name: Pretreatment residual lag covariance
definitions.construction: Set \(\widehat M^{\mathrm{pre}}=\mathcal P_r(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{I\times S})\), \(\widehat e_{is}=Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{is}-\widehat M^{\mathrm{pre}}_{is}\), and \(\widehat\gamma(h)=\{N(m-|h|)\}^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{s\in S:s+|h|\in S}\widehat e_{is}\widehat e_{i,s+|h|}\) for \(|h|\le q\).

definitions.name: Feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction
definitions.construction: For each target, use the declared \(\widehat Q_{it}\), \(\widehat\ell_{it}\), \(\widehat h_{it}\), and resulting \(\widehat q_{it}\) in the identical ordered \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\) chart. Then set \(\widehat B_2=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}[\widehat\gamma(0)\sum_{(j,u)\in\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}\widehat q_{it}(E^{it}_{ju})+\sum_{h=1}^q\widehat\gamma(h)\sum_{(j,s),(j,s+h)\in\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}\{\widehat q_{it}(E^{it}_{js}+E^{it}_{j,s+h})-\widehat q_{it}(E^{it}_{js})-\widehat q_{it}(E^{it}_{j,s+h})\}]\) and \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=\widehat\tau+\widehat B_2\).

definitions.name: Influence-weighted finite-lag variance and Wald interval
definitions.construction: Define \(\widehat w\) by \((gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\widehat\ell_{it}(R_{it}e)=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{s=1}^T\widehat w_{js}e_{js}\), where every \(\widehat\ell_{it}\) uses its declared ordered local chart. Set \(\widehat V=\sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{h=-q}^q\widehat\gamma(h)\sum_{s=1}^T\widehat w_{js}\widehat w_{j,s+h}\) and \(\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}=[\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V}]\).

definitions.name: Complete rank-one alternating-factor calibration array
definitions.construction: Along \(n\in8\mathbb N\), set \(N=T=n\), \(I=J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(G=\{1,\ldots,n/4\}\), \(S=\{1,\ldots,n/2\}\), \(W=\{n/2+2,\ldots,3n/4+1\}\), and \(C(t)=I\setminus G\). Hence \((N/n,T/n,m/n,g/n,H/n)=(1,1,1/2,1/4,1/4)\). For each target use \(I_{it}=C(t)\cup\{i\}\), \(J_{it}=S\cup\{t\}\), the increasing orderings, and \(R_{it}\); every target is at least two calendar periods after \(S\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}=\Omega\cap(I_{it}\times J_{it})=C(t)\times(S\cup\{t\})\;\cup\;\{i\}\times S\), with sole missing local coordinate \((i,t)\). Set \(r=q=1\), \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}=1/2<\sqrt{3/8}\), \(U_{i1}=u^{\mathrm{cal}}_i=n^{-1/2}\), \(p_t=p^{\mathrm{alt}}_t=1+\tfrac12(-1)^t\), \(V_{t1}=v^{\mathrm{cal}}_t=p_t/\sqrt{5n/4}\), \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), \(D=(\psi)\), \(M=UDV^{\top}\), \(\epsilon_{it}=z_{it}+\tfrac12z_{i,t-1}\) for independent \(z_{it}\sim N(0,1)\), and \(\lambda_n=4\sqrt n\,\log(n+2)\). The induced covariance is \(\gamma(0)=5/4\), \(\gamma(1)=1/2\), and \(\gamma(h)=0\) for \(|h|>1\). For \(t\in W\), \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}=\sigma_1(R_{it}M)=\psi\sqrt{(3/4+1/n)\{1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\}}\), so \(\inf_{i,t}\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi>c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and \(\kappa^{\mathrm{drift}}_t=-2\gamma(1)p_t(n/m)(1-\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)/(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)^{3/2}=-12p_t/(5\sqrt5)\).

definitions.name: Rank-one proximal-contraction frontier handle
definitions.construction: Expand the exact rank-one masked proximal fixed point over \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\) and derive each native-transfer, centered-quadratic, cubic, penalty, covariance-plug-in, Hessian-plug-in, and weight-plug-in bound as an explicit function of \(n,g,H,\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\). Substitute \(g\asymp n^b\), \(H\asymp n^c\), \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}n^a\), and \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\); state the resulting finite list of affine exponent inequalities and define \(\mathfrak F\) exactly as their intersection. For every exterior face, construct a relatively open positive-covariance Gaussian \(q\)-dependent rank-one family with \(|G_n|\asymp n^b\), \(|W_n|\asymp n^c\), and a positive local-to-global signal ratio, and prove that a named contraction fails at scale \(s\).

statements.statement: For every \((i,t)\in G\times W\), in the fixed ordered local space \(\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\), every native local optimizer satisfies the exact identity \(\widetilde M^{it}=\operatorname{SVT}_{\lambda}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}Y^{\mathrm{obs}}+P_{(\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it})^c}\widetilde M^{it})\). This identity holds for the implemented masked convex solution, not only for an auxiliary least-squares fit.
statements.justification: The fixed-point identity is the entry point for differentiating the actual estimator under neighborhood replacement.
statements.gap: Choi, Kwon, and Liao analyze an auxiliary-to-native bridge, but not this serial masked fixed point at second order.
statements.consumer: The native second-order transfer theorem uses the identity to keep every perturbation tied to the optimizer implemented in the Tick Size reanalysis.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \((i,t)\in G\times W\), for \(e\in\mathbb R^{I_{it}\times J_{it}}\), the first differential of the rank-\(r\) target-cell completion map at \(M^{it}=R_{it}M\) is \(\ell_{it}(e)=\sum_{j\in C(t)}a_{ij,t}e_{jt}+\sum_{s\in S}b_{t,s}e_{is}-\sum_{j\in C(t),s\in S}a_{ij,t}b_{t,s}e_{js}\). The minus donor-pre overlap term is part of the differential and is not a remainder.
statements.justification: A growing target window makes the overlap score load-bearing for both centering and variance.
statements.gap: The pointwise Choi--Yuan decomposition displays donor-window and treated-pre leading terms; it does not state this full three-term aggregate differential.
statements.consumer: The formula supplies the influence weights used by the finite-lag covariance estimator and prevents understated uncertainty for sustained policy effects.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P_n\) and \((i,t)\in G\times W\), the target-specific auxiliary fit \(\widehat M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}\) is \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\)-measurable, and \(\epsilon_{it}\perp\!\!\!\perp\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\mid(M,\Omega)\). The conclusion concerns the target noise coordinate; it does not assert independence between the entire deleted neighborhood and its complement.
statements.justification: Conditional row factorization and within-row block dependence give the exact sigma-field separation needed for target-specific leave-neighborhood conditioning.
statements.gap: Fully observed leave-neighbor PCA uses an analogous conditioning device, but the measurable object here is the output of a masked convex optimizer.
statements.consumer: The native transfer expansion can condition on the auxiliary fit without treating dependent neighboring noise coordinates as independent.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), first express all perturbation bounds through \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}=\inf_{(i,t)\in G\times W}\sigma_r(M^{it})\). The native and neighborhood-replaced fits satisfy \(|(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), and the native estimator obeys \((gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})=L+Q+R_{\mathrm{agg}}\), where \(|Q-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4/(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\sqrt n))\), \(|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\{\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+n^{-3/2}\})\), \(\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^2/\sqrt n)\), \(\Delta_\gamma=O_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt{\log n/m}+\log n/m+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}+\delta_{\mathrm{fit}}^2)\), \(|\widehat B_2-B_2|=O_{\mathbb P}(\ell_n^4\sqrt n/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2+\Delta_\gamma/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}})\), and \(\sum_i\|\widehat w_{i\cdot}-w_{i\cdot}\|_2^2=o_{\mathbb P}(s^2)\). The term \(R_{\mathrm{agg}}\) contains the cubic, penalty, and native-transfer components fixed by its definition. Since \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\le\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\le\psi\), substitution changes only constants. Under \(\psi\ge n^{1/2+\eta}H^{1/4}\ell_n^8\), the corresponding remainder-to-standard-error ratios are bounded by terms of orders \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\ell_n^4n\sqrt H/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}^2\), \(\ell_n^4\sqrt H/n\), and \(\Delta_\gamma\sqrt{nH}/\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\), all \(o_{\mathbb P}(1)\).
statements.justification: This is the unresolved bridge from a target-specific, conditionally independent neighborhood-replaced proof device to second-order inference for the native masked optimizer.
statements.gap: Choi, Kwon, and Liao prove first-order auxiliary equivalence under independent noise, while Choi and Yuan prove neighborhood deletion for fully observed PCA; neither controls this centered aggregate through a masked proximal map.
statements.consumer: The theorem certifies that feasible correction and studentization can be applied to the estimator already used for the SEC Tick Size Pilot panel.

statements.statement: On the complete rank-one alternating-factor calibration array with \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}=1/2\), let \(p_t=1+\tfrac12(-1)^t\). In the target chart \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\), the exact formula \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi=\sqrt{(3/4+1/n)\{1/2+4p_t^2/(5n)\}}\) implies \(\inf_{i,t}\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi>c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\) and \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}/\psi\to\sqrt{3/8}\). Direct contraction of the rank-one projector Hessian against the moving-average covariance in that same chart gives \(\psi_{\mathrm{loc},it}\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to-6\sqrt{3/2}\,p_t/(5\sqrt5)\), and therefore \(\psi\,\mathbb E[q_{it}(P_{\Omega_{\mathrm{loc}}^{it}}R_{it}\epsilon)\mid M]\to\kappa^{\mathrm{drift}}_t=-2\gamma(1)p_t(n/m)(1-\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)/(1+\rho_{\mathrm{alt}}^2)^{3/2}=-12p_t/(5\sqrt5)\) for every fixed parity of \(t\in W\). Thus the global-signal limits are \(-18/(5\sqrt5)\) for even targets and \(-6/(5\sqrt5)\) for odd targets, and \(\psi B_2\to-12/(5\sqrt5)\) because the consecutive window contains equally many targets of each parity. For the native masked optimizer with \(\lambda_n=4\sqrt n\log(n+2)\) and \(\psi=n^{4/5}\), the fitted correction removes this drift and \(n\{(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(\widehat M_{it}-M_{it})-L-\widehat B_2\}\to_{\mathbb P}0\).
statements.justification: The explicit parity constants replace an unsupported universal value and make the early kill test reproducible for the precise mask, factor normalization, dependence law, and penalty used by the native optimizer.
statements.gap: Neither the independent-noise MNAR theorem nor fully observed leave-neighbor PCA contains this masked rank-projection coefficient.
statements.consumer: A closed-form calibration case detects omitted interior overlap or regularization terms before empirical use.

statements.statement: The complete aggregate tangent weights implied by incoherence and the two normalized restricted-Gram bounds satisfy \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}s^{-2}\sum_{j\in I,s'\in J}w_{js'}^2=O(1)\) and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}s^{-1}\max_{j\in I,s'\in J}|w_{js'}|=o(1)\).
statements.justification: These structural weight bounds are the weighted-Lindeberg input and are derived from factor geometry rather than imposed as asymptotic normality.
statements.gap: The one-date subgroup theorem does not state score diffuseness uniformly over a growing cohort-window geometry.
statements.consumer: The dependency-graph central limit theorem and feasible studentization use these bounds to exclude domination by one noise coordinate.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\) when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\), the complete aggregate tangent weights implied by incoherence and the two normalized restricted-Gram bounds satisfy \(s^{-2}\sum_{j\in I,s'\in J}w_{js'}^2=O(1)\) and \(s^{-1}\max_{j\in I,s'\in J}|w_{js'}|=o(1)\).
statements.justification: The frontier weighted-Lindeberg bounds must adapt to both the treated-pre and donor-window variance components as \(b\) and \(c\) vary.
statements.gap: No checked weak-factor result derives score diffuseness uniformly over a three-exponent deterministic block-missing class.
statements.consumer: The frontier central limit theorem uses these bounds without fixing the cohort exponent at one.

statements.statement: Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), fixed \(q\), uniform sub-Gaussian moments, row-law factorization, conditional within-row block dependence, variance nondegeneracy, and the derived score-diffuseness bounds imply \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)|\to0\).
statements.justification: A uniform dependency-graph Lyapunov argument derives the Gaussian limit from primitive dependence, moments, and diffuse weights.
statements.gap: Existing serial factor central limit theorems do not cover this three-block influence array under deterministic causal-block masking.
statements.consumer: The Wald theorem uses this derived score limit instead of assuming asymptotic normality.

statements.statement: Conditional on \((M,\Omega)\), fixed \(q\), uniform sub-Gaussian moments, row-law factorization, conditional within-row block dependence, frontier variance nondegeneracy, and frontier score diffuseness imply \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P(L/s\le z\mid M,\Omega)-\Phi(z)|\to0\) uniformly when \((a,b,c)\) ranges over a compact subset of \([1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\).
statements.justification: A dependency-graph Lyapunov argument remains valid uniformly as the cohort and window exponents vary because the frontier weights are diffuse at their rescaled standard error.
statements.gap: Available serial factor central limit theorems do not provide this compact-uniform exponent-indexed statement for deterministic causal-block masking.
statements.consumer: The sharp-frontier achievability direction can focus on native-optimizer remainders rather than postulating a Gaussian leading score.

statements.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal P_n\), including sequences with \(H\to\infty\), \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau=-L+o_{\mathbb P}(s)\), \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), and the primitive conditional block-dependence and score-diffuseness conditions yield \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\mathbb P_P\{(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\le z\mid M,\Omega\}-\Phi(z)|\to0\). Consequently, \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}\mathbb P_P\{\tau\in\mathrm{CI}_{1-\alpha}\mid M,\Omega\}\to1-\alpha\). This strictly extends Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1, for the same native subgroup estimator from \(q=0,H=1\) to fixed \(q\ge1\), growing \(H\), and a feasible nonzero curvature correction.
statements.justification: The derived dependency-graph limit and feasible studentization convert weak-signal deterministic-MNAR completion into implementable inference for a sustained causal effect.
statements.gap: Choi and Yuan cover a one-date independent-noise subgroup average; Cen and Lam cover residual HAC for loading scores; Su, Wang, and Wang cover regression coefficients from alternating maximization.
statements.consumer: The confidence interval directly supports a reanalysis of the SEC Tick Size Pilot's average sustained liquidity effect over the realized treated cohort and post window.

statements.statement: In the special case \(q=0\) and \(H=1\), with the corresponding one-date Choi--Yuan subgroup conditions, \(B_2=o(s)\), the third overlap score is absorbed at their pointwise scale, and the standardized leading score and variance reduce to the group central limit theorem and variance formula in Choi and Yuan (2024), Theorem 3.1.
statements.justification: The reduction guards against changing the estimand or estimator while enlarging the dependence and target regimes.
statements.gap: The published theorem is the reduction target rather than an unresolved result.
statements.consumer: Applied users recover the existing one-date procedure when no serial or window correction is needed.

statements.statement: Characterize the sharp region \(\mathfrak F\) of exponent triples \((a,b,c)\in[1/2,1]\times(0,1]\times[0,1]\) for which the primitive class \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\), with global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\asymp n^a\), local comparability \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\), \(g\asymp n^b\), \(H\asymp n^c\), and \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\asymp n^{-1-\min\{b,c\}}\), permits oracle-scale curvature-corrected native-optimizer inference. Derive raw bounds for every native-transfer, centered-quadratic, cubic, penalty, covariance-plug-in, Hessian-plug-in, and weight-plug-in remainder as functions of \(n,g,H,\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\); after exponent substitution, define \(\mathfrak F\) exactly by the resulting affine inequalities that make every remainder divided by \(s\) vanish. On every compact subset of its interior, prove \(s^{-1}|(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}\Delta^{\mathrm{aux}}_{it}|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|Q-B_2|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|R_{\mathrm{agg}}|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), \(s^{-1}|\widehat B_2-B_2|\to_{\mathbb P}0\), and \(\widehat V/s^2\to_{\mathbb P}1\), together with the studentized limit. For every exterior boundary face, construct a relatively open rank-one Gaussian \(q\)-dependent family with \(|G_n|\asymp n^b\), \(|W_n|\asymp n^c\), and \(\inf_{i,t}\sigma_1(R_{it}M)/\sigma_1(M)>0\), satisfying the remaining primitive conditions, on which one named native-optimizer error is not \(o_{\mathbb P}(s)\).
statements.justification: The sufficient proportional-cohort envelope is useful but does not locate the statistical or algorithmic boundary when signal, cohort, and window exponents all vary.
statements.gap: Existing papers provide separate sufficient weak-factor conditions or bias-aware impossibilities, not a matched native-optimizer frontier over the exponent-indexed class with the two-component oracle variance scale.
statements.consumer: The frontier determines whether a desired Tick Size post window must be shortened, the treated cohort subdivided, or the reported interval declared unsupported.

sampling_model.design: A deterministic common-start treatment block \(G\times W\) removes untreated potential outcomes from the completion sample; inference is conditional on the mask and the low-rank signal.
sampling_model.units: Conditional on the signal, row laws factor across units. Within each row the centered sub-Gaussian process has common stationary covariance and genuine finite-range block dependence with fixed known \(q\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treated outcomes \(Y_{it}(1)\) are observed on \(G\times W\); their counterfactual mean component \(M_{it}\) is imputed from donor and pretreatment observations.
sampling_model.overlap: Donor and pretreatment factor Grams have explicit normalized eigenvalue bounds, and every target restriction retains at least the fixed fraction \(c_{\mathrm{loc}}\) of the global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\). The proportional-cohort theorem has score variance of order \((nH)^{-1}\); the exponent-indexed frontier class has variance \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Known rank is used in the native local nuclear-norm and rank-projection fits. Every target-specific native and auxiliary fit uses the same ordered \(I_{it}\times J_{it}\) chart and restriction map \(R_{it}\). A target-specific auxiliary fit measurable with respect to \(\mathcal G_{it}^{(-t)}\) supports leave-neighborhood conditioning. Pretreatment residuals estimate finite-lag covariance, while fitted tangent weights and fitted projector Hessians estimate variance and serial curvature.
sampling_model.randomness: All probability statements are with respect to the rowwise error processes, conditional on \(M\), \(A\), and the realized treated potential outcomes.

estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}=(gH)^{-1}\sum_{i\in G,t\in W}(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{it}-\widehat M_{it})+\widehat B_2,\quad (\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{bc}}-\tau)/\sqrt{\widehat V}\Rightarrow N(0,1)\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Subgroup nuclear-norm completion permits inference for imputed entries under a large deterministic missing block and independent errors.
Leave-neighbor-out analysis gives weak-factor principal-component normality under dependent noise in a fully observed matrix.
Auxiliary leave-one-out estimators are asymptotically equivalent to the feasible nuclear-norm-based estimator without sample splitting.
Residual HAC estimators consistently estimate covariance matrices for weak-factor tensor loading scores with missing observations.
Convex and nonconvex matrix-completion solutions are tightly coupled under independent random entry sampling.
Double-debiased matrix completion yields confidence intervals for general linear forms under random entry sampling.
Residual block bootstrap confidence intervals cover fixed-cell treatment effects under weakly dependent factor errors.
Adjusted principal components provide pointwise factor and loading inference with general missing observations and dependent errors.
Factor and loading limit distributions are derived under general missing-data patterns.
Bias-aware confidence intervals attain uniformly correct coverage over weak interactive effects for admissible regressors.
Analytically bias-corrected alternating maximization is asymptotically normal for regression coefficients under unbalanced interactive effects.

tldr: A growing post window makes serial dependence enter deterministic-MNAR panel completion twice: through the long-run variance of the complete three-block tangent score and through a nonzero quadratic drift of rank projection. The kernel derives both objects for the implemented Choi--Yuan subgroup nuclear-norm estimator in target-indexed local charts, transfers a target-specific conditionally independent auxiliary fit through its masked proximal fixed point, estimates variance and drift from pretreatment residuals, and derives a uniform studentized limit under a global weak-signal envelope and fixed local-to-global signal comparability. A separate primitive class \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\) leaves the sharp signal--cohort--window frontier open with \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\) and no inherited remainder envelope.

project_justification.gap: Deterministic-MNAR panel completion has weak-signal inference only under independent errors and small one-date subgroups. Dependent-noise PCA, residual HAC for missing factors, and analytic bias correction for unbalanced interactive-effects regression do not control the implemented masked convex completion estimator at the shrinking standard-error scale of a growing causal window.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a native-optimizer second-order expansion whose first differential retains donor-window, treated-pre, and donor-pre overlap terms and whose projector curvature is contracted against finite-lag covariance.
project_justification.fill: The project supplies a local-signal-indexed native expansion, a feasible Hessian--lag covariance correction defined in the same target chart as each auxiliary fit, an influence-weighted residual covariance estimator, a dependency-graph central limit theorem derived from conditional block dependence and factor-geometric score diffuseness, and uniform Wald coverage. A separate exponent-indexed class poses the sharp signal--cohort--window frontier without building a sufficient remainder envelope into its assumptions.

related_work: Choi and Yuan (2024) establish the same subgroup nuclear-norm and rank-projection architecture for deterministic-MNAR blocks; Theorem 2 strictly extends their one-date independent-noise limit, and Proposition 2 records the exact reduction. Choi and Yuan (2025) informs target-specific leave-neighbor conditioning for weak fully observed PCA; the present conditioning claim uses row-law factorization and genuine within-row block dependence and does not assert independence of a deleted neighborhood from its complement. Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) informs the coupling of a proof-only leave-out fit to an implemented convex estimator. Chen et al. (2020) informs entrywise control of an actual convex matrix-completion solution under a different sampling design. Cen and Lam (2025) informs the residual-HAC feasible-oracle decomposition for missing weak-factor scores. Xia and Yuan (2021) informs the tangent-projection expansion for linear matrix functionals under random sampling. Xiong and Pelger (2023) and Su and Wang (2025) give pointwise or factor-score inference under general missing patterns, with different estimators and factor regimes. Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024) obtain fixed-cell bootstrap intervals rather than an analytic growing-window law. Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) obtain weak-factor-uniform bias-aware regression intervals but exclude the common-start subset policy regressor. Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) derive analytic missing-pattern bias corrections for alternating-maximization regression coefficients; that result does not cover a rank-projected completed-cell aggregate or its serial curvature. Ben-Michael and Feller (2026) motivate the aggregation last mile but do not state the native second-order theorem. A public theorem text for the 2026 Choi--Yuan rejoinder was not located, so it is not a load-bearing comparator.
technical_internal_limitation: The presolve identities and rank-one calculations are diagnostic evidence, not established results. The decisive unresolved step is uniform second-order transfer through the native masked optimizer, including centered quadratic aggregation, active-singular-space stability, penalty error, cubic terms, and feasible plug-in error at scale \(s\). Every perturbation bound must first be uniform in \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\); global-signal rates follow only after applying \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\). The score-diffuseness and dependency-graph lemmas must be derived from the stated factor geometry and conditional block dependence. If the rank-one Gaussian moving-average kill test leaves a nonvanishing interior term after correction, or if transfer requires \(\psi\asymp n\), the stated theorem must be withdrawn rather than weakened silently.
honest_scope: The proved-rate proposal class conditions on exact known fixed rank, fixed known dependence range, conditionally independent rows, genuine within-row finite-range block dependence, a common stationary covariance, a fixed positive local-to-global signal comparability constant, a proportional treated cohort, bounded aspect ratios, and explicit donor/pre restricted-Gram bounds. It covers a realized cohort-window contrast with a growing but non-proportional-at-the-noise-boundary window. The separate frontier class varies \(g\asymp n^b\), \(H\asymp n^c\), and the global signal \(\psi=\sigma_r(M)\asymp n^a\), retains only \(\psi_{\min,\mathrm{loc}}\ge c_{\mathrm{loc}}\psi\) and the other primitive geometric and moment conditions, uses \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\), and does not inherit the proved theorem's signal-window envelope or any negligible-remainder condition. Its window growth remains subject to \(W\subset J\), consecutiveness, and placement after \(S\). The project does not claim simultaneous event-time bands, unknown-rank validity, heterogeneous row covariance, hidden-block identification, rank overprojection robustness, or proportional-window inference when \(\psi\) is arbitrarily close to \(n^{1/2}\). The native transfer, feasible correction, coverage theorem, and sharp frontier are open; only their proof handles and falsification cases are specified.

seed_details.title: Native-optimizer curvature-corrected limit law for a growing-window causal contrast
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, Section 3 and equation (3.1), Theorem 3.1, Proposition C.1 and its proof, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2308.02364 were read. The paper proves one-date subgroup inference for the rank-projected nuclear-norm estimator under independent errors; its proof exposes two leading score blocks and leaves serial dependence outside the theorem.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the pointwise independent-noise decomposition after rank projection by a uniform second-order expansion of the masked singular-value-thresholding fixed point. The target-specific auxiliary fit must be measurable outside the row-\(i\) \(q\)-neighborhood, the first derivative must retain all three score blocks, and the second derivative must be centered and corrected under finite-range block dependence.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches pairing deterministic block missingness, native nuclear-norm optimization, weak factors, serial dependence, growing post windows, and analytic curvature correction found no theorem with the full conjunction. Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) is the closest new collision, but its target is an interactive-effects regression coefficient and its final estimator is alternating maximization.
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Choi and Yuan (2024) plus a finite-lag HAC because the target is only an average of their imputed cells.
seed_details.rebuttal: The published theorem is one-date and independent-noise; serial covariance creates a nonzero rank-projection quadratic drift, while growing aggregation promotes the omitted donor-pre differential and native-optimizer transfer error to the oracle standard-error scale.

seed_details.title: Sharp signal--cohort--window frontier for oracle-scale panel inference
seed_details.anchor_opened: The subgroup-size restrictions in Theorem 3.1, the weak-signal discussion in the Introduction, the decomposition in Proposition C.1, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2308.02364 were read. They establish an achievability region for small subgroups but do not characterize a three-way frontier for a growing consecutive window.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Work over the separate class \(\mathcal P_n(a,b,c)\), track every inverse singular-value power and every cohort-window contraction relative to \(s^2\asymp(nH)^{-1}+(ng)^{-1}\), and match the upper region with relatively open rank-one Gaussian finite-range-dependent families having \(|G_n|\asymp n^b\) and \(|W_n|\asymp n^c\).
seed_details.destination_search: Choi and Yuan (2025) index higher-order PCA remainders by signal strength; Armstrong, Weidner, and Zeleneev (2026) give weak-factor-uniform bias-aware regression inference; Xia and Yuan (2021) treat growing-support linear matrix forms under random sampling. None gives this native masked-optimizer three-way frontier.
seed_details.red_team: The frontier is merely the sufficient rate condition in Choi and Yuan rewritten with a window size.
seed_details.rebuttal: The frontier class replaces the theorem's sufficient envelope by \(\psi\asymp n^a\) and varies both cohort and window exponents; a sharp result requires native-optimizer upper bounds and nondegenerate serial exterior families, neither of which follows by substitution into a pointwise condition.
seed_details.disposition: retained as the first-class open-ended question

seed_details.title: Influence-weighted residual finite-lag covariance and Hessian-drift estimation
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, the loading-row central limit theorem, the two residual covariance constructions in Section 4, Theorem 4.3 and its proof discussion, and the terminal discussion of arXiv:2403.13153 were read. Its feasible HAC result concerns tensor loading scores and explicitly does not deliver common-component normality.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Decompose feasible-minus-oracle lag contractions into centered residual products, estimated influence weights, and native masked-optimizer contamination, then reuse the same lag estimates inside the second Fréchet-derivative drift.
seed_details.destination_search: Adjacent results by Xiong and Pelger (2023), Li, Shen, and Zhou (2024), and Su and Wang (2025) cover pointwise imputation, bootstrap intervals, or loading-row inference. None estimates both the aggregate score variance and a projection-Hessian drift for the Choi--Yuan estimator.
seed_details.red_team: Cen and Lam's residual HAC theorem applies after replacing their loading score by the ATT influence score.
seed_details.rebuttal: The ATT weights are estimated from overlapping masked optimizers and also enter a serial quadratic bias; the required feasible-oracle decomposition contains optimizer contamination and Hessian terms absent from their loading-row proof.

seed_details.title: Equivalence frontier between leave-neighbor auxiliary and native masked convex fits
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, the auxiliary leave-one-out construction in Section 4, the feasible central limit theorem, the estimator-equivalence lemmas and their proofs, and the Conclusion of arXiv:2307.16370 were read. The auxiliary object is proof-only and is coupled to the implemented estimator under independent noise.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Differentiate the implicit masked proximal KKT map with respect to a whole serial neighborhood rather than delete one observation from a least-squares refit.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi and Yuan (2025) supplies neighborhood deletion for fully observed PCA, while Chen et al. (2020) supplies a convex-to-nonconvex bridge under random entry sampling. No exact observed-primitive divergence frontier for the causal block was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is the same leave-one-out equivalence lemma with a larger deleted set.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deleting a serial neighborhood perturbs the active singular spaces and the imputed part of the masked fixed point globally, so second-order aggregate equivalence is not implied by the pointwise lemma.
seed_details.disposition: dropped as a proof theorem rather than a stand-alone causal kernel

seed_details.title: Analytic-Wald versus block-bootstrap divergence for aggregated panel effects
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, estimator construction, cellwise coverage theorem and proof, block wild bootstrap algorithm, and Conclusion of arXiv:2202.12078 were read. The proof lets the treated-cell shock dominate pointwise imputation error.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: For a growing window, replace the single treated shock by an influence-weighted serial sum and compare conditional bootstrap centering with the analytic projection-curvature correction.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper was found deriving an observed-primitive equivalence boundary between these two procedures for a weak-factor deterministic block. The available bootstrap target is nevertheless not the same structural cohort-window contrast.
seed_details.red_team: Standard block-bootstrap validity and Slutsky already imply equivalence with a consistent analytic variance estimator.
seed_details.rebuttal: That argument does not determine whether the bootstrap reproduces the estimator's serial quadratic centering, but the comparator's cellwise estimand makes the proposed frontier insufficiently clean.

seed_details.title: Growing-support linear-form inference under deterministic masking and serial noise
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, double-debiasing construction, Theorem 4 and its alignment discussion, spectral-projector expansion in the proof, and terminal discussion of arXiv:1909.00116 were read. The theorem handles general linear forms under independent random entry sampling.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace random-sampling tangent isotropy by explicit donor and pre restricted Grams, then retain serial covariance contractions of the second spectral-projector derivative.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination pair of structured linear forms and deterministic causal masks is partially approached by Choi and Yuan (2024), but no general serial theorem was found.
seed_details.red_team: This is Xia and Yuan's linear-form theorem with deterministic weights.
seed_details.rebuttal: Deterministic block masking changes the inverse tangent operator and adds serial curvature, but the generic target sacrifices the concrete causal consumer available for the ATT kernel.
seed_details.disposition: dropped in favor of the concrete cohort-window target

seed_details.title: Weak-factor-uniform bias-aware inference for a common-start policy block
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, nuclear-norm error theorem, minimax-linear construction, uniform confidence theorem and proof architecture, the common-start policy-indicator exclusion, and terminal discussion of arXiv:2210.06639 were read.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace regression residualization, which fails under low-rank collinearity of a common-start indicator, by counterfactual block completion with donor/pre restricted-Gram identification.
seed_details.destination_search: The search confirmed that the anchor deliberately excludes the relevant policy indicator. Choi and Yuan (2024) identifies the block through completion, but combining that identification with factor-uniform bias-aware inference would require a different full model.
seed_details.red_team: The anchor's exclusion is an identification failure, so changing the estimator cannot restore uniform inference without new information.
seed_details.rebuttal: Donor/pre span restrictions can supply that information, but doing so changes the published model enough that this is a separate, less feasible project.

seed_details.title: Serial growing-window inference for all-purpose missing-factor PCA
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, adjusted-covariance estimator, pointwise common-component theorem, average-effect discussion, proof decomposition, and Conclusion of arXiv:1910.08273 were read. The estimator accommodates general missingness and dependence but uses a different PCA geometry.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Aggregate its pointwise loading and factor expansions over a consecutive causal window and retain cross-time score covariances at the aggregate scale.
seed_details.destination_search: Su and Wang (2025) advances general-missing factor inference, and Su, Wang, and Wang (2026) adds unbalanced-panel regression inference. Neither targets the Choi--Yuan weak-signal convex estimator.
seed_details.red_team: Weighted averages are already covered by summing the published pointwise influence functions.
seed_details.rebuttal: Uniform remainder and serial covariance control do not follow from pointwise expansions, but the estimator switch moves away from the topic's implemented procedure.
seed_details.disposition: dropped for consumer and estimator mismatch

seed_details.title: Leave-neighbor perturbation theory for an implicit masked proximal map
seed_details.anchor_opened: The Introduction, leave-neighbor-out construction in the dependent-noise section, the weak-factor central limit theorem, recursive perturbation proof, and Conclusion of arXiv:2402.05789 were read. The method replaces a time neighborhood by signal in fully observed PCA.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Apply neighborhood replacement inside the imputed singular-value-thresholding fixed point and control changes of its KKT system and active singular subspaces.
seed_details.destination_search: Choi, Kwon, and Liao (2024) bridges an auxiliary object to a convex initializer, and Chen et al. (2020) controls an actual convex matrix-completion solution. Neither combines masked proximal sensitivity with serial neighborhood replacement.
seed_details.red_team: The implicit-function theorem for a spectrally separated proximal fixed point gives the result mechanically.
seed_details.rebuttal: The observation projector destroys global strong convexity and the growing signed aggregate requires uniform second-order, penalty, and active-space control beyond local differentiability.
